# Agba

> Agba is executive operating intelligence for growing businesses. It connects signals across departments, remembers company context, detects what changed, and tells leadership what deserves attention.

## Primary website
- https://agba.work/

## What is Agba?
Agba is an intelligence layer for growing companies. Department heads report what is happening in their areas, and Agba connects those updates across the business so leadership can understand the whole company in context.

## What does Agba do?
- Connects Finance, Sales, Operations, HR and other department signals.
- Remembers important company context across reports and conversations.
- Detects relationships, changes and business risks that span departments.
- Surfaces what deserves executive attention.
- Helps leadership move from reporting to decisions and follow-up.

## How does Agba work?
Agba follows an executive operating loop: Report, Understand, Connect, Remember, Alert, Decide and Follow up. A department update becomes more useful when Agba can relate it to earlier context and signals from other parts of the company.

## Who is Agba for?
Agba is designed for founders, CEOs, managing directors and operators of growing businesses whose information is becoming fragmented across departments.

## Does Agba replace department reporting?
No. Agba is designed to make existing reporting more useful. Teams can report naturally, including through Telegram, while Agba connects the information for leadership.

## Can teams use Telegram with Agba?
Yes. Telegram can be used as a reporting and conversational surface. Agba can retain the relevant company context and connect updates across teams.

## What makes Agba different from a dashboard?
Agba is not positioned as a conventional dashboard of vanity metrics. Its purpose is to connect company signals, preserve context, identify what changed and surface decisions or exceptions that deserve attention. Business intelligence dashboards can remain complementary for detailed metrics and analysis.

## Executive example
Operations reports that a supplier is three days late. Sales has already promised the customer a Friday delivery. Finance confirms that the customer has paid. Agba connects those signals and surfaces the delivery risk so leadership can act before the issue becomes a surprise.
